threads.label: Strait of Hormuz closure and economic war
threads.summary: Regime channels and Iran International reported Tehran framing the Strait of Hormuz as 'non-negotiable' and amplifying foreign coverage of closed shipping lanes, fuel-supply concerns in Europe and rising US petrol prices. Defa Press described the Iran-US confrontation as having shifted into a maritime and economic phase, while Khamenei's office published a review of Mojtaba Khamenei's views on managing the waterway.

threads.label: US and UK sanctions on Iran oil trade
threads.summary: The US State Department announced sanctions on multiple entities, an individual and a vessel involved in Iranian petroleum and petrochemical trade, including Qingdao Haiye Oil Terminal, targeting the Iran-China oil route. The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office republished statutory guidance for the Iran, Iran nuclear and Yemen sanctions regimes on 1 May.

threads.label: Khamenei Workers' Day and Teachers' Day message
threads.summary: Khamenei's office released a message from Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei marking Workers' Day and Teachers' Day, calling on Iran to move from military proof of capability into 'economic and cultural jihad' and urging businesses to avoid layoffs. The office also asked Iranians to prioritise domestically-produced goods, with the message issued in text, audio and video formats on 1 May.

threads.label: Executions and detained dissidents in Iran
threads.summary: Iran International and Defa Press reported that Yaqoub Karimpur and Naser Bakrzadeh were hanged on Saturday after the Supreme Court upheld death sentences for alleged espionage for Israel and the Mossad. Iran International also reported that jailed Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi was hospitalised from Zanjan Prison after losing consciousness twice.

threads.label: Post-war domestic strain in Iran
threads.summary: Iran International reported inflation above 73 per cent, a surging dollar and US naval pressure heightening official concerns about internal instability, and said Tehran residents displaced by the 40-day war with the US and Israel were ordered out of temporary hotel housing. A separate report described pressure on Ottawa to explain how Iran football chief Mehdi Taj, a former IRGC intelligence officer, briefly entered Canada.

events.summary_en: Trump faces difficulty replacing munitions consumed in the war with Iran, according to a report by the New York Times: Trump's plans to increase weapons production may not yield results for years. The programme faces serious obstacles including lack of certain funding and failure to pass Congress, and even if approved, many of these advanced weapons require long production times. Experts say rebuilding weapons stockpiles and reaching desired production levels could take years.

events.summary_en: Politico: Europe doesn't even know how much fuel it has. Fear of supply shortage is growing faster than the European Union's ability to measure it. Europe's efforts to prevent shortages resulting from the war with Iran have faced an unexpected obstacle: nobody knows exactly how much fuel the continent has. This blind spot may render them unable to identify shortages or force them to make emergency decisions based on incomplete information.

events.summary: Dozens of residents in Tehran displaced by a 40-day war with the US and Israel said municipal authorities ordered them to vacate temporary hotel housing despite unsafe homes and limited aid, according to interviews published by Etemad newspaper on Thursday.

events.title: Ottawa on defensive after Iran football chief linked to IRGC entered Canada
